layers.note: Mostly a subcanopy and gap tree under conifers; reaches the canopy on moist bottoms, streamsides and in openings.

moisture.note: Moist, well-drained soil: stream terraces, floodplain edges and lower slopes; not waterlogged ground.

heat_load.note: Grows on most aspects at low elevation; scarce on the coolest north-east slopes.

elevation_m.note: Commonest below about 450 m in western Washington; scattered higher.

max_slope_deg.note: Grows on slopes, most often on lower ones.

shade_tolerance.note: Moderately shade tolerant: persists under conifers and sprouts from stumps.

coldest_c.note: Across its range (see the provenance note), coldest-month means from about −3 °C, gone by −7 °C, up to about 13 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −22 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −30 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 14.5 to 25 °C; gone below 12 °C, where summers are too short, and above 28.5 °C.

degree_days_0.note: A long cool growing season: about 2,300 or more degree-days above 0 °C, none below 1,500.

degree_days_5.note: About 1,000 or more degree-days above 5 °C, none below 550: the warmth of the maritime lowlands and lower mountain slopes.

moisture_index.note: A humid climate: a moisture index from about 0.55 (gone by 0.4), wet winters filling the soil through a dry summer.

summer_rain.note: The summer-dry Pacific climate: no lower limit; its range lies where at most about 0.4 of the year's precipitation falls in summer.

provenance.notes: Authored from general knowledge of the species in western Washington lowland forests; not yet checked against Silvics of North America (Burns and Honkala, 1990) or the Fire Effects Information System, both public-domain USDA Forest Service works. Climate ranges (niche schema 2, 2026-10-06): Bigleaf maple grows from south-west British Columbia to southern California, near the coast and in the Sierra Nevada's foothills (Silvics of North America, vol. 2). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range at the 2.8° ERA5 product's scale, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records.
